name: Defender DLP — Bulk Sensitive-Data Movement by a Single User
description:
Attacker objective
Exfiltrate a large volume of sensitive data — here, cardholder/PCI documents — by copying or uploading many distinct files, whether by a malicious insider or a compromised account.

Attack logic
Routine business use produces a small number of DLP matches per user. A single user triggering DLP on many distinct sensitive documents within a short window indicates bulk data movement, not incidental handling.

Why this detection works
Aggregating distinct DLP-matched documents per user over the alert stream distinguishes bulk exfiltration from the routine single-document matches that make per-alert DLP rules unusable.

False positives
A user performing a legitimate bulk migration/reporting task; a shared account.

Tuning
Set the distinct-document threshold above the routine per-user rate; allowlist sanctioned bulk-processing accounts; correlate with the destination (upload/USB/print) in the DLP evidence.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (detection_source=DLP, title=document, user.name, evidence.device_dns_name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The user moved many distinct sensitive documents; review the document list and the DLP action (block/audit).
2. Confirm business justification; if none, treat as insider data exfiltration and involve fraud/risk and HR.
3. Check the user's device and account for compromise (correlate with Defender/Windows detections).
false_positives: A user performing a legitimate bulk migration/reporting task; a shared account.
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.alert* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE m365_defender.alert.detection_source == "microsoftDataLossPrevention" AND user.name IS NOT NULL AND NOT user.name IN ("Unknown","LOGIN","-")
| STATS documents = COUNT_DISTINCT(m365_defender.alert.title), alerts = COUNT(), devices = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name) BY user.name
| WHERE documents >= 10

name: Defender — Endpoint Incident Spanning Multiple Attack Tactics
description:
Attacker objective
Progress an intrusion on one endpoint or incident across several attack stages — for example malware execution followed by persistence, discovery, or lateral movement.

Attack logic
Microsoft Defender groups related alerts into an incident per entity. An incident that spans two or more distinct non-DLP attack tactics represents a genuine, multi-stage compromise rather than an isolated detection.

Why this detection works
Aggregating distinct Defender tactics per incident (excluding the DLP/exfiltration class) confirms multi-stage activity that any single Defender alert cannot, with low false-positive risk.

False positives
A single behaviour that Defender maps to two adjacent tactics; a noisy test/UAT host generating varied benign detections.

Tuning
Exclude verified test/UAT incidents; raise the distinct-tactic threshold for higher confidence.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (incident_id, threat.tactic.name, title, evidence, severity, user.name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the incident in the Defender console; the tactics/titles show the attack progression.
2. Identify the device and user; treat as an active multi-stage compromise — isolate and begin IR.
3. Correlate the device/user with Windows/AD detections for corroboration and scope.
false_positives: A single behaviour that Defender maps to two adjacent tactics; a noisy test/UAT host generating varied benign detections.
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.alert* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE threat.tactic.name IS NOT NULL AND threat.tactic.name != "Exfiltration" AND m365_defender.alert.incident_id IS NOT NULL
| STATS tactics = VALUES(threat.tactic.name), distinct_tactics = COUNT_DISTINCT(threat.tactic.name), titles = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.title), devices = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name), users = VALUES(user.name), severities = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.severity) BY m365_defender.alert.incident_id
| WHERE distinct_tactics >= 2

name: Defender — High-Confidence Endpoint/Identity/Office Attack Alert
description:
Attacker objective
Establish or extend a foothold — exploit a public-facing service, deliver malware, create a rogue account, or compromise an identity — surfaced by Microsoft Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365).

Attack logic
Defender's Endpoint/Identity/Office sensors apply cloud-scale analytics and raise a discrete alert on genuine attacker activity. Unlike the DLP and bulk-antivirus streams, these three sources correspond to real intrusion behaviour and are low-volume.

Why this detection works
Scoping to the Endpoint/Identity/Office sources (excluding DLP/bulk-AV and resolved alerts) surfaces every high-confidence Defender detection, and derives the device short-name and user so the alert can be correlated with Windows, AD and perimeter detections on the same entity.

False positives
A Defender benign-positive or a sanctioned red-team exercise (e.g. an authorised scanner triggering an exploitation alert).

Tuning
Triage against the Defender determination; suppress verified benign detections by title or actor; escalate high severity and privileged-user/critical-server alerts.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (detection_source, severity, status, title, evidence.device_dns_name, user.name, threat.tactic.name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Open the Defender alert and review the title, evidence entities and MITRE techniques.
2. Identify the device/user; for exploitation or account-creation alerts, treat the entity as compromised pending triage.
3. Correlate with the Windows/AD and perimeter detections on the same user/host.
false_positives: A Defender benign-positive or a sanctioned red-team exercise (e.g. an authorised scanner triggering an exploitation alert).
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.alert* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE m365_defender.alert.detection_source IN ("microsoftDefenderForEndpoint","microsoftDefenderForIdentity","microsoftDefenderForOffice365") AND m365_defender.alert.severity != "informational" AND m365_defender.alert.status != "resolved" AND NOT user.name IN ("nessus")
| EVAL host.name = MV_FIRST(SPLIT(TO_LOWER(MV_FIRST(m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name)), "."))
| KEEP @timestamp, user.name, host.name, m365_defender.alert.title, m365_defender.alert.severity, m365_defender.alert.detection_source, m365_defender.alert.incident_id, threat.tactic.name, m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name

name: Microsoft Defender / MDI — Credential Access Behavior (Kerberoasting / Ticket Abuse / Pass-the-Hash / Spray)
tags: Data Source: Microsoft Defender for Identity
description: Fires when Microsoft Defender XDR or Microsoft Defender for Identity (MDI) reports ANY Credential-Access behavior for ANY account — Kerberoasting (SPN exposure / TGS harvesting), suspicious Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ, over-Pass-the-Hash, DFS coercion, or password-spray. Identity-agnostic redesign of the Defender-consuming coverage: the previous new_terms 'New Entity' rule fired only once per never-before-seen entity and required high severity, so a sustained single-tactic credential-access campaign produced NO Elastic alert even though every event was a high-fidelity Defender/MDI detection. This rule promotes every Credential-Access detection into a SOC-worked alert. Portable About: works on any tenant shipping logs-m365_defender.* via the Elastic Microsoft 365 Defender integration; keys only on ECS threat.tactic.name + event.kind, no host/user/index specifics.
note:
## Triage
1. Open the Defender/MDI incident via `m365_defender.alert.incident_web_url`.
2. Identify the **actor** (`user.name`/`user.email`) and **target** (`m365_defender.alert.evidence[].hostName`).
3. Behavior = `m365_defender.alert.title` / `m365_defender.alert.detector_id`:
   - `KerberoastingSecurityAlert` / `xdr_PossibleKerberoastingAttack` -> Kerberoasting (T1558.003)
   - `xdr_SusKerberosAuth_AsReq` / `xdr_SusKerberosAuth_TgsReq` -> anomalous Kerberos ticketing (T1558/T1550)
   - `xdr_PossibleOverPassTheHash` -> Pass-the-Hash (T1550.002)
   - `xdr_RiskyLoginByTitanPasswordSprayIp` -> password spray (T1110.003)
4. Confirm whether the actor is an approved pentest identity before closing.
author: raadabujaish
false_positives: Authorized red-team / penetration-test engagements (validate against the engagement window and scope).
Security tooling that legitimately performs Kerberos ticket requests at volume (validate the source account).

name: Microsoft Defender / MDI — Active Directory Reconnaissance (LDAP / SPN / ADCS / SAMR / DNS Enumeration)
tags: Data Source: Microsoft Defender for Identity
description: Promotes every Microsoft Defender for Identity / XDR **Discovery** detection into a SOC-worked Elastic alert, for ANY account — AD Certificate Services enumeration, LDAP search reconnaissance, SPN enumeration via LDAP, security-principal (SAMR/LDAP) reconnaissance, DNS reconnaissance, and Kerberoasting LDAP recon. These are the pre-attack mapping steps (BloodHound/SharpHound/ldapsearch/Certipy-find) that precede credential theft and lateral movement. NBI had NO rule consuming Defender Discovery alerts; the native equivalents are blind here — 4662 DS-access is buried under thousands of legitimate admin/DirSync reads, and AD CS auditing (4886-4900) is not collected at all. Identity-agnostic: keys only on ECS threat.tactic.name + event.kind. Portable to any tenant shipping logs-m365_defender.* via the Elastic Microsoft 365 Defender integration.
note:
## Triage
1. Open the Defender/MDI incident (`m365_defender.alert.incident_web_url`).
2. Actor = `user.name`; targets = `evidence[].deviceEvidence` (usually the DCs).
3. `detector_id`: `xdr_PossibleActiveDirectoryCertificateServicesEnumeration` = ADCS recon (ESC hunting); `LdapSearchReconnaissanceSecurityAlert`/`xdr_PossibleSpnEnumerationLdap` = BloodHound/SPN mapping; `SamrReconnaissanceSecurityAlert` = SAMR enum; `DnsReconnaissanceSecurityAlert` = DNS zone recon.
4. Recon against DCs from a non-admin or unmanaged host is a strong pre-attack indicator — pivot to the same actor's Credential-Access alerts and 4624 logon spread.
author: raadabujaish

name: Defender — New Host Exhibiting Malware or Hacktool Activity
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise a new endpoint with malware, a hacktool, or unwanted software as part of an intrusion.

Attack logic
Persistent malware detections on the same test/UAT or research host are recurring background noise. A device that has not previously shown malware and now does is a fresh infection worth immediate triage.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the device auto-baselines the set of hosts that habitually generate malware detections and fires only when a genuinely new host appears — turning a noisy stream into a high-signal one.

False positives
A newly onboarded lab/test host, or a first benign EICAR/test detection on a new device.

Tuning
Exclude verified lab/test devices; the history window auto-baselines recurring-detection hosts.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (threat.tactic.name, evidence.device_dns_name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the newly-flagged device and the malware/hacktool family.
2. Confirm it is not a known lab host; if production, isolate and scan, and correlate with Windows process/persistence detections.
false_positives: A newly onboarded lab/test host, or a first benign EICAR/test detection on a new device.

name: Defender — User Flagged by Multiple Defender Products
description:
Attacker objective
Operate as a compromised identity whose malicious activity is independently observed by more than one Microsoft Defender sensor.

Attack logic
When two distinct Defender products (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, antivirus) independently flag the same user, the corroboration sharply increases the likelihood of a genuine compromise over a single-sensor false positive.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct Defender detection sources per user, across the real-attack sensors, elevates cross-sensor agreement into one high-confidence alert.

False positives
A power user whose legitimate activity independently trips two sensors; shared/service accounts.

Tuning
Exclude verified shared/service accounts; require a specific high-value source (Endpoint/Identity) if noisy.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (user.name, detection_source, title, threat.tactic.name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The user was flagged by multiple Defender products — review each product's alert and evidence.
2. Correlate with the user's Windows/AD activity (logons, privileged changes) and contain the account if compromise is confirmed.
false_positives: A power user whose legitimate activity independently trips two sensors; shared/service accounts.
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.alert* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE user.name IS NOT NULL AND NOT user.name IN ("Unknown","LOGIN","-","System","SYSTEM") AND m365_defender.alert.detection_source IN ("microsoftDefenderForEndpoint","microsoftDefenderForIdentity","microsoftDefenderForOffice365","antivirus")
| STATS sources = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.detection_source), distinct_sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(m365_defender.alert.detection_source), titles = VALUES(m365_defender.alert.title), tactics = VALUES(threat.tactic.name) BY user.name
| WHERE distinct_sources >= 2

name: Microsoft Defender XDR — High-Volume Data Exfiltration Activity (Single Entity)
description: Raises an alert when a single entity accumulates 50 or more Microsoft Defender XDR Exfiltration alerts within the window, indicating anomalous outbound data-movement activity. The alert surfaces the alert count, maximum severity, source IPs, techniques, and sample Defender messages.
note:
## Investigation
1. Review `threat_details` and `techniques` to see what data-movement Defender flagged.
2. Determine whether `account` is a legitimate high-volume data mover (backup/ETL/reporting) or an anomaly.
3. Check destination of the transfers and correlate with FortiGate egress + endpoint for the same window.
4. If unexplained, treat as potential data exfiltration.
author: raadabujaish
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.*
| MV_EXPAND threat.tactic.name
| WHERE threat.tactic.name == "Exfiltration"
| STATS exfil_alerts = COUNT(*), max_severity = MAX(event.severity), source_ips = VALUES(source.ip),
        techniques = VALUES(threat.technique.subtechnique.id), threat_details = VALUES(message),
        device_id = VALUES(host.id), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY account = user.name
| WHERE exfil_alerts >= 50
| SORT exfil_alerts DESC

name: Microsoft Defender XDR — Multi-Stage / High-Impact Threat Correlation (Single Entity)
description: Correlates Microsoft Defender XDR alerts by entity (the user, or the device when no user is present) and raises a high-severity alert when a single entity shows EITHER three or more distinct ATT&CK tactics within the window (multi-stage activity) OR at least one high-severity alert in a high-impact tactic — Exfiltration, Credential Access, or Lateral Movement. The alert surfaces the correlated tactics, techniques, source IPs, the underlying Defender alert messages, and the first/last activity time.
note:
## Investigation
1. Read `threat_details` (the underlying Defender alert messages), `tactics`, and `techniques` to see exactly what was detected.
2. `account` / `device_id` identify the entity; `source_ips` and `first_seen`/`last_seen` give origin and time window.
3. If >=3 tactics: treat as a multi-stage attack on one entity. If high-severity Credential Access / Exfiltration / Lateral Movement: prioritise accordingly.
4. Pivot to Windows 4688, PowerShell 4104, and FortiGate for the same account/host and window.
5. Confirm whether the account is authorised security testing before closing; otherwise isolate and rotate credentials.
author: raadabujaish
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.*
| EVAL entity = COALESCE(user.name, MV_FIRST(host.id))
| MV_EXPAND threat.tactic.name
| STATS defender_alerts = COUNT(*),
        distinct_tactics = COUNT_DISTINCT(threat.tactic.name),
        tactics = VALUES(threat.tactic.name),
        high_impact_alerts = COUNT(*) WHERE (event.severity >= 73 AND threat.tactic.name IN ("Exfiltration","CredentialAccess","LateralMovement")),
        max_severity = MAX(event.severity),
        source_ips = VALUES(source.ip),
        techniques = VALUES(threat.technique.subtechnique.id),
        threat_details = VALUES(message),
        account = VALUES(user.name),
        device_id = VALUES(host.id),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen = MAX(@timestamp)
        BY entity
| WHERE distinct_tactics >= 3 OR high_impact_alerts >= 1
| SORT high_impact_alerts DESC, distinct_tactics DESC

name: Microsoft Defender XDR — New Entity Entering High-Severity High-Impact Status
description: Raises an alert when a user appears for the first time (not observed in the previous 7 days) within a high-severity (severity >= 73) Microsoft Defender XDR alert in a high-impact tactic — Exfiltration, Credential Access, or Lateral Movement. Identifies a new account entering severe-threat status.
note:
## Investigation
1. This is a NEW entity crossing into severe status — treat as a potential fresh compromise.
2. Read the Defender `message`/`threat.technique`; identify `source.ip` and whether the account is privileged.
3. Pivot to endpoint (4688/4104) and FortiGate for the entity and window.
4. Confirm whether the account is authorised security testing before closing.
author: raadabujaish

name: M365 — Impossible Travel (Distant Successful Logins)
description: Detects a single user successfully authenticating to Microsoft 365 from two geographically distant locations within a window too short to physically travel between them (derived from O365 audit GeoIP) — indicating account compromise or credential sharing.
false_positives: Users on a corporate VPN that egresses through different countries
Travelling employees connecting via airport WiFi (different GeoIP
Mobile-network routing — some carriers' GeoIP localises across
query:
FROM logs-o365.audit-default
| WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 60 minutes
  AND event.action == "UserLoggedIn"
  AND event.outcome == "success"
  AND user.name IS NOT NULL
  AND source.ip IS NOT NULL
  AND source.geo.country_iso_code IS NOT NULL
| STATS countries  = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.geo.country_iso_code),
        seen       = VALUES(source.geo.country_iso_code),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen  = MAX(@timestamp),
        sources    = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip)
        BY user.name
| WHERE countries >= 2
| EVAL window_minutes = DATE_DIFF("minutes", first_seen, last_seen)
| WHERE window_minutes <= 60 AND window_minutes > 0
| SORT countries DESC
| KEEP user.name, countries, seen, sources, first_seen, last_seen, window_minutes
